The session journal documents a terminal session as a readable timeline: every server output line and every command you type is written to a capture log, an AI periodically condenses the activity into short journal entries, and the result is rendered as a self-contained HTML page with connection details, color-coded excerpts, screenshots and your own notes. Journals are managed like saved chats — in their own manager window with search, editing and export.
Each journal is one self-contained directory under KTPH000 (configurable in KTPH001Settings KTPH003 Logging KTPH004 Session JournalKTPH002):
The curated journal document: metadata, AI summaries, markers, notes, screenshot references
The append-only capture log — timestamped server output and typed input lines with sequence ids
Rotated log parts; closed parts are gzip-compressed automatically, the journal never deletes history
The generated timeline page, regenerated automatically after every change
Screenshots you attached during the session

The capture-log format is selectable in the journal manager's KTPH002OptionsKTPH003 dialog: KTPH004JSONKTPH005 (JSON Lines, the default), KTPH006XMLKTPH007 or KTPH008YAMLKTPH009. All formats carry the same fields, and every entry is exactly one line, so a crash never corrupts more than the last line. JSON is the default because it is the smallest of the three once a finished part is compressed, and because log tooling reads it without needing a parser of its own; XML is a few percent smaller uncompressed, and YAML is the largest, since it writes JSON mappings with a KTPH000 prefix. The active log part stays uncompressed for live reads; rotation (default 25 MB per part) and session end compress finished parts to KTPH001.
Open KTPH000Connections KTPH002 Manage ConnectionsKTPH001 and edit a connection
On the KTPH000JournalKTPH001 tab, enable KTPH002Enable session journal for this connectionKTPH003
Optionally adjust KTPH000Capture typed input linesKTPH001, KTPH002Generate AI summariesKTPH003 and the per-connection KTPH004Summary intervalKTPH005
Every future connection of this server then starts its journal automatically. The journal survives reconnects — one journal per tab lifetime, with a reconnect marker in the log.

Use KTPH003Tools KTPH015 Start/Stop Session JournalKTPH004 (KTPH005KTPH000KTPH006+KTPH007KTPH001KTPH008+KTPH009KTPH002KTPH010), the tab context menu (KTPH011Session Journal KTPH016 Start journalKTPH012) or the journal bar's KTPH013Start journalKTPH014 button. The existing scrollback is imported into the journal as seed entries first, so the timeline covers what already happened, then live capture attaches.

While a journal is available, a bar below the terminal shows its state (KTPH000Journal active since HH:MMKTPH001) and offers KTPH002Stop journalKTPH003, KTPH004ScreenshotKTPH005 and KTPH006NoteKTPH007:

KTPH003ScreenshotKTPH004 (KTPH005KTPH000KTPH006+KTPH007KTPH001KTPH008+KTPH009KTPH002KTPH010, also in the terminal's right-click menu) snapshots the terminal — in a split layout, the right-click menu captures exactly the pane under the cursor — and files it into the journal timeline.
KTPH000NoteKTPH001 opens a small input for a free-text remark that appears as its own timeline entry at the current position.

While the journal runs, the AI summarizer periodically reads the newest capture-log lines and appends a compact journal entry (title, summary and a suggested marker: info, important or error). Defaults and limits:
KTPH000Settings KTPH002 Logging KTPH003 Session JournalKTPH001 (global) or per connection
Max. terminal lines per AI evaluation
Journal manager KTPH000OptionsKTPH001, visible when max lines is 0
Journal manager KTPH000OptionsKTPH001 or KTPH002Settings KTPH004 Logging KTPH005 Session JournalKTPH003

Summaries use your KTPH000default AI profileKTPH001 unless you pick a dedicated journal profile. That choice is available in three equivalent places: the journal manager's KTPH002OptionsKTPH003 dialog, KTPH004Settings KTPH008 Logging KTPH009 Session JournalKTPH005, and KTPH006AI KTPH010 AI Manager KTPH011 Local AIKTPH007 next to the Text and Coding roles. The Text/Coding role profiles themselves are deliberately not used for the journal.

Setting KTPH000max lines to 0KTPH001 switches to context filling: the summarizer packs as many of the newest lines as fit into the configured token budget. With KTPH002chunkingKTPH003 enabled the whole backlog is processed instead of only the newest window — consecutive windows of the configured size, one AI prompt each.
Chunking can take very long on large sessions and is not recommended for everyday use — it is intended for power users with capable hardware and a powerful LLM.

When the session ends, the summarizer writes a closing KTPH000session summaryKTPH001 entry (what was accomplished, which errors occurred). Optionally — KTPH002Let the AI title the journal when the session endsKTPH003 in the Options dialog — a final AI call names the journal, unless you renamed it manually.

The journal works without AI: if no AI profile is available, AI features are disabled, or summaries are switched off, the timeline records raw activity entries instead. AI summary prompts never use internet-access tools; the terminal excerpt goes only to the configured AI profile.
Typed input is captured only as complete submitted lines, and several layers keep passwords out of the journal:

When the server output ends in a password prompt (KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002, KTPH003, and localized variants), the next submitted input line is suppressed and logged as a redacted placeholder — the typed text is never buffered or written.
The connection's own stored password is additionally replaced by KTPH000 wherever it would appear in captured text.
KTPH000Capture typed input linesKTPH001 can be disabled per connection entirely; commands then only appear as the server's echo in the output stream.

The prompt detection is a heuristic — a remote terminal cannot reliably know when the server disabled echo. Exotic or full-screen password prompts may not be recognized, and secrets pasted into visible commands (other than the connection's own credentials) are captured like any other text. Treat journals of sensitive sessions accordingly.

If something slipped through anyway, the viewer's KTPH000search and replaceKTPH001 removes it from the entries and the capture log after the fact. Administrators can also have korTTY redact patterns automatically — see KTPH002Enterprise policyKTPH003 below.
KTPH000 is fully self-contained (no external resources) and works in the built-in viewer, in any browser, and inside the exported bundle:

A sticky header shows who was connected to which server, start time, duration, and counts for entries, commands, errors and screenshots, plus the journal description. Live journals show a KTPH000liveKTPH001 badge. The line below the title only carries what the title does not already say, so a journal named after its endpoint states the connection once instead of three times.

The timeline groups entries by day; each entry carries its time, a colored marker dot/badge (red = error, amber = important, blue = info), the AI title and summary, and color-coded input (green) and output (blue) excerpts.

Clicking an entry slides a log panel in from the bottom with the exact capture-log range behind that entry. The panel has its own scrollbar, a search field with a match counter and ▲/▼ navigation (KTPH004KTPH000KTPH005 / KTPH006KTPH001KTPH007+KTPH008KTPH002KTPH009 also cycle matches, KTPH010KTPH003KTPH011 closes), and colors input and output lines differently.
Screenshot entries show thumbnails; clicking one opens a full-size lightbox.
The page renders dark by default, follows the system light/dark preference and has its own theme toggle.

Screenshots, excerpt panels, the timeline column and the log panel size themselves to the window, so the page stays readable in a narrow viewer tab as well as full screen. Long excerpts scroll inside their own box instead of stretching the timeline.

The magnifier in the header opens a search bar directly under the connection details (KTPH006KTPH000KTPH007+KTPH008KTPH001KTPH009 works too). Typing a term or a whole sentence highlights every occurrence across the timeline — entry titles, AI summaries, input and output excerpts, notes and timestamps — and shows a match counter; ▲ and ▼ or KTPH010KTPH002KTPH011 / KTPH012KTPH003KTPH013+KTPH014KTPH004KTPH015 jump between the hits, KTPH016KTPH005KTPH017 or ✕ closes the bar and clears the highlighting.

This searches the journal entries. The raw capture log has its own search inside the log panel, and the journal manager can search across KTPH000allKTPH001 journals with KTPH002Search contentsKTPH003.

Every entry carries a copy button in its top-right corner: text entries copy the whole entry, screenshot entries copy the image. The log panel has the same button for the log section it currently shows.
Right-clicking the page opens a copy menu with more targeted actions, depending on what you clicked:
The currently selected text (shown whenever a selection exists)
The entry's time, title and AI summary
The same plus the input/output excerpts and your note
The screenshot itself, as an image, onto the clipboard
The screenshot's path inside the journal folder
Every line of the log range currently shown in the panel, with timestamps

Inside korTTY the copy actions use the app's clipboard, so images land on the system clipboard ready to paste. In an external browser text still copies normally; copying an image may fall back to its path, because browsers block reading local image data from a KTPH000 page.

The KTPH000A−KTPH001, KTPH002AKTPH003 and KTPH004A+KTPH005 buttons in the page header scale the whole page between 70 % and 250 %. korTTY remembers the size and applies it to every journal page it renders afterwards, so a page that regenerates (a new AI summary, an edited marker) comes back at the size you chose. Opened standalone in a browser the page remembers the size per browser instead.

KTPH003Tools KTPH011 Session Journals…KTPH004 (KTPH005KTPH000KTPH006+KTPH007KTPH001KTPH008+KTPH009KTPH002KTPH010) opens the journal manager: all journals in a table sorted by start time (newest first) with duration, connection, server, title and entry count. Running journals are marked and cannot be renamed or deleted while live.

The filter field matches title, connection, host, user and description; enabling KTPH000Search contentsKTPH001 additionally scans the journal entries and capture logs of every journal in the background.

KTPH000OpenKTPH001 (or double-click) opens the journal viewer; KTPH002RenameKTPH003 changes the title; KTPH004DeleteKTPH005 asks for confirmation and then permanently removes the journal folder including the log and all screenshots.
Several journals can be selected at once (KTPH002KTPH000KTPH003 / KTPH004KTPH001KTPH005 click) to delete or export them in one step. Running journals cannot be renamed or deleted.
The KTPH000DescriptionKTPH001 area below the table stores a free-text description per journal; it appears on the journal page and in every export and is included in the content search.
KTPH000OptionsKTPH001 holds the global capture and AI settings described above.

The viewer shows the journal page in an embedded browser and refreshes automatically while the journal is still being written. KTPH000Open in browserKTPH001 hands the page to your system browser. KTPH002EditKTPH003 splits the view: an entry table next to a form with the entry's KTPH004TitleKTPH005, KTPH006SummaryKTPH007, a marker choice (KTPH008None / Info / Important / ErrorKTPH009) and a notes field. Editing lets you correct or categorize entries — flag failures, highlight important findings, or rewrite a summary. Saving regenerates the page at the edited entry's position; a marker you set manually is never overwritten by the AI.

Searching finds a term. KTPH000Search KTPH002 replaceKTPH001 rewrites every occurrence. Use it to erase something that must not stay in the journal — a password pasted into a visible command, a token in a server response — or simply to correct a recurring word.

It is reachable from two places: the KTPH000Search KTPH008 replace…KTPH001 button in edit mode, and the KTPH002Replace…KTPH003 button in KTPH004the search bar on the journal pageKTPH005, which opens the same dialog with the term you were searching for already filled in. That button only appears inside korTTY — the page is generated KTPH006fromKTPH007 the journal files, so a copy opened in a browser can search but has no way to rewrite anything.
The text to find and what to put in its place (KTPH000 by default)
Treats the search text as a regex; KTPH000 in the replacement inserts a captured group
KTPH000Rewrite the capture log as wellKTPH001
On by default. Off changes only the journal entries and leaves the raw log untouched
A dry run over the real journal: reports how many entry fields and log lines KTPH000wouldKTPH001 change, without writing anything

Replacing covers every entry title, AI summary, note and excerpt, and — unless you turned it off — every capture-log part including the compressed ones. The file header and every untouched line are preserved exactly, so the log keeps its structure.

Replacing rewrites the journal files in place and cannot be undone. Use KTPH000Count matchesKTPH001 first, especially with a regular expression. Documents you already exported are separate files and are not changed — export them again afterwards. A journal that is still being written cannot be rewritten; stop the session first.
The search text is never written to korTTY's own log, because for a redaction it KTPH000isKTPH001 the secret.

KTPH000Delete entryKTPH001 removes the selected timeline entry after a confirmation, and a screenshot entry's image file with it. It does not touch the capture log — to remove a text from there as well, use Search KTPH002 replace.
The KTPH000ExportKTPH001 menu in the manager and the viewer offers three formats:
The simple journal: header with connection details and statistics, day-grouped entries with marker badges, input/output excerpts, notes — and, if selected, downscaled embedded screenshots
The same simple journal as a KTPH000 file; screenshots are copied into a sibling KTPH001 folder
A zip archive of the whole journal — KTPH000, KTPH001, the decompressed capture logs and all screenshots — laid out so the page works immediately after unzipping
PDF and Markdown ask whether screenshots should be included.

With more than one journal selected, the export writes a single zip archive that keeps each journal separate: one PDF or Markdown document per journal, or one folder per journal for the HTML bundle. Names are taken from the journal titles, with a numeric suffix if two titles collide.

Every archive — including the HTML bundle of a single journal — can be KTPH000protected with a passwordKTPH001. The option sits in the export dialog and encrypts the archive with KTPH002AES-256KTPH003; without it the archive is written unencrypted. Journals contain full terminal transcripts, so an unprotected archive is a deliberate choice.
The password is not stored anywhere. korTTY cannot recover an encrypted archive if you lose it.

By default every exported document carries a footer stating that it was created with korTTY, with a link to the project repository — at the bottom of each PDF page, at the end of the Markdown file, and in the footer of the journal page inside the HTML bundle. PDFs can additionally carry a diagonal watermark, which is KTPH000off by defaultKTPH001.

Both are configured under KTPH000KTPH001Configuration → Global Settings → ExportKTPH002KTPH003, where you can change the footer text, turn the footer off, enable the watermark and choose its text and colour. The same settings apply to AI chat exports.

Administrators can deny the feature (KTPH000 under KTPH001), or mandate its behavior via KTPH002: force a journal for every connection, fix the log format, AI line window or storage directory, forbid renaming or deleting journals, prescribe a naming template and enforce the closing AI title. See KTPH003Enterprise policyKTPH004 for the keys.

A KTPH000 list makes korTTY apply search-and-replace automatically, with regular expressions if the administrator wants them — for cloud access keys, internal hostnames, ticket numbers, anything that must never end up in a transcript:

These rules run on the capture thread, before a line is written, so a matching text never reaches the log file in the first place; they are applied to AI summaries and notes as well. Every rule of every matching policy tier applies — a rule adding a pattern never switches another one off. The dialog above tells you how many mandated rules are in force. Journals written before a rule existed are not rewritten retroactively; use Search KTPH002 replace for those. See KTPH000Enterprise policyKTPH001 for every key.
